reasoning_traces.think:
The core methodology integrates three distinct but complementary statistical frameworks. First, the Markov Switching Model (MSM) identifies discrete states of team spatial behavior—offensive, defensive, or transitional—by detecting shifts in the geometric properties of player positions. This is essential for capturing non-stationary dynamics in team sports. Second, the convex hull area serves as a geometric proxy for team coordination and spatial distribution, enabling quantification of how players collectively occupy space. Third, the Vector Auto Regressive (VAR) model bridges the gap between these behavioral regimes and measurable outcomes such as points scored. The integration allows for temporal reasoning where spatial configurations predict performance outcomes. Failure modes include overfitting in VAR due to high dimensionality, loss of convex hull validity when players cluster, and misclassification in MSM due to noise in tracking data. These primitives form a dual framework: one for detection and categorization (MSM), another for quantification and prediction (VAR), with geometric constraints (convex hull) anchoring both.
